purpose: Exact, machine-readable reproduction reference for a from-scratch rebuild (Stage 7B.2a). NOT acceptance criteria: build honestly, and if results diverge, investigate and report -- never change code/parameters merely to reproduce these.

A_hybrid_probe_contract_7b2a.description: Stage 7B.2 / 7B.2a hybrid Vector-Graph probe. ONE immutable global algorithm configuration + the decision gates, declared BEFORE the measured run. Contains NO question-specific paths, seeds, answers, or relationship hints, and permits NO per-question tuning. The final per-question evidence budget (top_k) comes ONLY from the frozen Stage 7B.0 question contract, never from here.

parameter_notes.max_supplemental_seed_nodes: Global cap on supplemental (Vector-chunk + semantic-edge) seed nodes retained per query, AFTER RRF-ranking supplemental node candidates by their Vector-chunk source rank and semantic-edge source rank. Every explicit-alias seed is ALWAYS retained (never capped). No per-question seed limits.
parameter_notes.supplemental_seed_saturation_threshold: Benchmark qualification fails if selected supplemental seeds exceed this fraction of the eligible graph node count -- EXCEPT when the eligible graph has <= 4 nodes (a small graph is legitimately saturated).
parameter_notes.path_enumeration_safety_ceiling: Path enumeration must fail explicitly if the number of authority-eligible simple paths (no repeated node, <= max_hop_depth) exceeds this global ceiling. It is a safety bound, NOT a truncation of candidates before scoring.
parameter_notes.max_candidate_paths: The number of paths RETAINED after ALL enumerated paths are embedded and semantically ranked. It is applied ONLY after semantic ranking, never as an early DFS cutoff.

modes.V: Frozen authority-aware Vector baseline (Stage 7B.0 result, loaded, never rerun/rescored).
modes.G: Frozen Stage 7B.1 simple Graph baseline. For the real graph this is the committed Stage 7B.1 per-question Graph result, verified by exact equality of ranked chunk ids/ranks/scores before use.
modes.H0: Reciprocal-Rank-Fusion of the frozen Vector ranking with the simple-Graph ranking.
modes.H1: H0, but the Graph side traverses from EXPANDED seeds (explicit-alias always + up to max_supplemental_seed_nodes RRF-ranked Vector-chunk/semantic-edge supplemental seeds), hop-distance-ranked.
modes.H2: H1, but the Graph side enumerates ALL eligible simple paths, semantically ranks every one by query<->path-representation cosine, and retains the top max_candidate_paths (not hop distance).

graph_conditions.real_graph: The exact committed Stage 7B.1 measured graph snapshot (loaded from reports/stage7b1_graph_build_results.json; OpenAI extraction is NOT rerun).
graph_conditions.perfect_graph: The deterministic FakeRelationshipExtractor graph (recall 1.00, precision 1.00, 0 normalization collisions).

decision_gates.note: Exactly one decision is returned. Gates are evaluated in the fixed order A, B, D, C and are NOT altered after seeing results. Zero authority leakage, the same final K as Vector, and no query-time LLM are HARD SAFETY REQUIREMENTS for A, B, and D -- a mode failing any of them cannot satisfy those gates. 'target questions' are Q04/Q06/Q07 (deep/distributed chain); a 'complete-chain improvement' means H2 makes complete_chain_represented true where the frozen Vector baseline had it false.

C_authority_setup_timelines.description: Per logical document, replayed through Stage 7R.1's own unmodified contract_runner._run_registry_setup + service. Symbols are globally unique across documents so one shared symbol_to_id map is safe. Every rev1 became effective 2020-01-01; each current successor superseded it effective 2023-01-01; the draft control (ctl_rev3) is registered but never activated (stays draft).

C_revision_authority_scenarios.description: Deterministic Stage 7R.1/7R.1a authority-resolution contract -- not a replacement for source-document fixtures. Every 'symbol' below is a local alias the runner resolves to a real compute_document_revision_id() hash after replaying registry_setup; scenarios reference revisions by symbol. Stage 7R.1a: effective dates now live SOLELY in AuthorityPeriod, opened/closed via activate/reinstate/withdraw -- 'decide' registry_setup steps are pure publication_status changes, never dates.

logical_documents.description: One resilience/retention policy document: superseded, historical, current, draft, under_review, approved-future, a rollback-corrected candidate, and a late-uploaded draft.

revisions.note: exact duplicate registration of v3 (Scenario A)
Scenario F: registered very late (2026), never activated -- must not become current merely by existing

logical_documents.description: Scenario K: a document whose only effective revision is withdrawn (at an explicit withdrawal_effective_date, never recorded_at) with no replacement registered.

Scenario L: two revisions simultaneously effective. Stage 7R.1a's own pre-activation overlap validation now correctly PREVENTS this via ordinary service calls -- so this precondition is constructed via one legitimate activation plus one raw, low-level repository write (op=corrupt_period), simulating pre-existing inconsistent data (e.g. from before this validation existed) rather than a mistake the service itself could still be tricked into making.
Scenario N: identical textual content (source_document_sha256) reused under a DIFFERENT logical_document_id -- must get a fully independent revision identity.

logical_documents.description: Stage 7R.1a item 3: v3 effective from 2023-01-01, v5 effective from 2028-01-01 (supersedes v3), v5 rolled back on 2028-06-01, v3 reinstated from 2028-06-01 -- a SECOND, disjoint authority period for v3.

A revision left in publication_status='draft' but given a REAL (non-zero-width) authority period via a raw repository write -- the exact 'effective revision is not approved' integrity violation, constructed directly (never reachable via normal service calls) to prove comparison/draft intents exclude it individually rather than aborting the whole query.
Item 5: activation validation rejections, proven directly against the service (each step below is EXPECTED to raise).

pre_effective_authority_correction, isolated: v6 approved-future then retracted before it ever took effect (closure_reason=correction, zero-width period) -- kept in its own document since it never needs to interact with any other revision's own period.

query_scenarios.description: A newer draft (v4) exists but must not replace the current effective revision (v3).
v5 is approved with a future effective_from (2028-01-01); as of 2027-12-31 it must NOT be current.
On the exact effective_from boundary (2028-01-01), v5 becomes effective and v3 becomes superseded in the SAME atomic transition.
One day before the boundary (2027-12-31), the OLD revision (v3) is still effective -- end-exclusive interval semantics.
v0 is registered very late (2026) but never approved/activated -- late upload alone must never grant currency.
Plain current-authoritative query -- exactly one eligible revision.
Historical as-of query resolves the revision that was effective THEN, not now.
Item 2: as_of BEFORE the withdrawal date, within the old (now-closed) period, must still resolve effective.
Comparison permits superseded/current/future revisions together, retaining their own labels -- never silently picking one.
Draft intent returns only the explicitly requested draft/under_review revisions -- v3 (effective, not draft) is excluded even though explicitly requested, never silently mixed in.
under_review is ALSO a legitimate draft-intent result -- v4_under_review must be eligible.
current/as_of ON/AFTER the withdrawal date: fails closed, never silently returns nothing as if that were a normal empty result.
Two revisions simultaneously effective -- fails closed rather than silently choosing one.
v6 was approved-future then RETRACTED (closure_reason=correction) before it ever took effect -- comparison shows it back in draft, and the correction never touches v3/v5's own effective windows.
Byte-identical content under a DIFFERENT logical_document_id gets a fully independent revision identity.
Item 3: as_of 2027-12-31 (before rv5 ever existed) -> rv3.
Item 3: as_of 2028-03-01 (rv5's own window, before rollback) -> rv5.
Item 3: current/as_of 2028-07-01 (after rollback) -> REINSTATED rv3, rv3's own SECOND authority period.

A revision with a genuinely malformed record (draft status + a real, non-zero-width period -- 'effective revision is not approved') is EXCLUDED individually under comparison intent, never aborting the whole query.
The SAME malformed revision is EXCLUDED individually under draft intent too, never aborting the whole query.
Item 6: requesting the same revision id twice under comparison intent deduplicates deterministically -- one eligible entry, one duplicate_request exclusion, never two eligible entries.

authority_snapshot.description: Declarative registry setup -- reuses the SAME registry_setup step vocabulary (register/activate) as contracts/revision_authority_scenarios_v2.json, replayed through Stage 7R.1's own, unmodified contract_runner._run_registry_setup and service.py. v1 -> v2 -> v3 is a straight supersession chain; v4 and v5 are registered but left in draft (v5 is activated later, ONLY by the authority_switch step below).

queries.description: Scenario A: plain current query -- exactly v3 (7 years) is eligible; v1/v2 historical, v4 draft, v5 an unactivated candidate must never appear.
queries.query: How long must customer account records be retained after account closure?

queries.description: Scenario B: an as_of query dated inside v2's own authority window (2018-01-01..2022-01-01) resolves v2 (5 years), never the currently-effective v3.
queries.query: How long must customer account records be retained after account closure?

queries.description: Scenario C: an explicit draft-intent query for v4 returns v4 (proposed 10 years), visibly labeled draft -- never treated as current authority.
queries.query: How long must customer account records be retained after account closure?

queries.description: Scenario D: an explicit comparison query for v2 and v3 returns EXACTLY those two, each with its own value and its own authority label -- never merged, never a third revision.
queries.query: How long must customer account records be retained after account closure?

authority_switch.description: Scenario E: v3 is effective; v5 is already ingested/chunked/embedded and registered as a candidate (draft). Run the current query (records v3). Activate v5 (effective_from == this query's as_of_date), superseding v3 -- NO re-ingestion, re-chunking, or re-embedding of anything. Run the SAME current query again with the SAME as_of_date (records v5). Only the registry snapshot hash and the eligible/search results may change; the index itself (row count, content hash, chunk ids/hashes, stored vectors, embedding-call count) must be byte-identical before and after.

query.query: How long must customer account records be retained after account closure?
